claim: Humans mix model-free and model-based signatures in the Daw two-step task (median model-based weight 0.39 in N=17), and a hybrid with a weight fits better than either pure system. But the hybrid label is contested (see K02). [Gap search: Feher da Silva Table 1 medians re-read: Daw 0.39, Kool 2016 0.24, spaceship 0.78, carpet 0.79.]
agent_test: Compare always-reason, always-direct and a mixture at equal tokens; check the mixture beats both.

claim: The hybrid reading is not safe: with story-based instructions people look mostly model-based (median w 0.78-0.79 vs 0.24-0.39 in earlier data), and a purely model-based agent with a wrong task model is labelled hybrid. Low model-basedness can be a misunderstanding of the task, not habit. [Gap search: all six numbers (0.24, 0.39, 0.78, 0.79 observed; 0.94, 0.36 simulated) confirmed on the preprint v1 PDF; 0.80 also reported for a second wrong-model agent. Spaceship N=21, carpet N=24.]
agent_test: Give the agent the task model as plain story vs bare rules; measure whether it plans more at equal tokens.

claim: Model-free agents can mimic model-based stay-probability signatures (latent states, history), and chunked action sequences can mimic model-free choice. The classic two-step signature is not diagnostic of planning.
agent_test: Judge whether our agent planned from outcomes on changed-reward probes, not from surface traces.

claim: In the original two-step task model-based control earns almost no extra reward (0.52 at w=0, +0.002 at w=1), so it cannot test cost-benefit arbitration. Redesigned tasks where planning pays raise median w (0.27 to 0.48).
agent_test: Build task bins (planning pays / does not) and check the gate decides differently by bin.

claim: People use more model-based control when it pays more and when stakes are higher (incentive effect d=0.35, N=839). Evidence of cost-benefit arbitration in humans. Kool 2017 itself was seen only in snippets. [Gap search: Kool 2017 now opened. Exp 1 N=98, w 0.76 vs 0.54, d=0.47; replication N=93, d=0.29. Exp 2 N=100 with no payoff gap: d=-0.04. Instructions were extensive with comprehension checks. A 2026 sample (n=140) also shows learned arbitration.]
agent_test: Vary a reward-for-accuracy multiplier and check the gate raises reasoning depth only when gain is real.

claim: Arbitration by value of information versus time cost (Keramati 2011): plan only if the value of perfect information exceeds average reward rate times deliberation time. Extended to depth and direction of search (Sezener 2019). Theory with qualitative simulations only.
agent_test: Implement the gate: expected gain from a slow pass (from fast-answer uncertainty) vs token cost; compare with fixed thresholds.

claim: Uncertainty-based arbitration (Daw 2005): trust the controller with lower value uncertainty; planning wins early and near reward, cache wins late. Simulation only.
agent_test: Use disagreement among cheap samples as the uncertainty signal for the gate.

claim: Humans plan to limited depth then plug in cached values (plan-until-habit); time pressure (700 ms vs 2 s, n=15 per group) makes planning shallower. [Gap search: design re-read (n=15 vs 15; plan-until-habit effect only after unrewarded trials, P<0.002; rewarded P=0.073). No larger replication found in 137 citing records. Stays single-source.]
agent_test: Allow cached-answer plug-in at depth k; compare with full-depth reasoning under a token cap.

claim: Load and stress reduce model-based control: cold-pressor stress with cortisol rise (N=48 analysed, low working-memory people hit) and a concurrent Stroop load (Otto 2013, snippet only). [Gap search: Otto 2013 now opened: 43 recruited, 25 analysed, t(24)=2.94; no large replication found; tDCS n=22 null is a different manipulation.]
agent_test: Add distractor load to context; check whether the agent drifts to shallow cached answers.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: More model-based learning predicts later sensitivity to outcome devaluation (N=90, replicated N=95): model-based use protects against habit. Note a21 gives wrong authors; correct is Gillan, Otto, Phelps, Daw 2015.
agent_test: Background only: caches harden with repetition; check repeated-task shortcuts stay valid.

claim: Model-based deficits track a compulsivity/intrusive-thought dimension, not diagnostic categories (N=548, replication N=1413).
agent_test: None for the agent; background.

claim: Rival accounts of habit exist: direct action strengthening (Miller 2019), action chunks (Dezfouli and Balleine 2013), and the claim that the MB/MF split is too coarse (Collins and Cockburn 2020).
agent_test: Treat the dual-system split as a design metaphor; test the gate empirically.

claim: Always-plan LLM agents are not best: intermediate planning frequency beats always-plan and never-plan (Crafter, POGS, 100 seeds). Trained Llama-3.1-8B reaches 0.387 vs 0.379 for 70B zero-shot with 85% fewer output tokens (1,714 vs 11,510). Imagine-then-Plan finds adaptive lookahead beats fixed/random. [Gap search: Paglieri zero-shot Crafter 70B: never 0.343 at 560 tokens, every 4 steps 0.379 at 11,511, always 0.349 at 38,836. Goldilocks shapes differ by model; Imagine-then-Plan adaptive beats fixed-k and random at matched budget.]
agent_test: Sweep replan interval k at equal tokens; expect a peak at intermediate k.

claim: Reasoning models overthink easy items: 1,953% more tokens than conventional models on 2+3; first correct solution at 39 of 901 tokens (4.3%). AdaptThink cuts length 53.0% with +2.4 accuracy (1.5B). Thinkless similar.
agent_test: Route easy items to direct answer; measure tokens saved at equal accuracy.

claim: Confidence-based gates give small gains: fast answer first then slow call on 8.20% of items gives +1.02 points (47.90 to 48.92) vs random same-budget routing 46.76, but cost-aware utility did not beat always-fast (0.4731 vs 0.4789). A separate router misjudges the target model's difficulty (Thinkless). [Gap search: He and Feng Table 1 re-read: random -1.14, avg log-prob +0.32, logit gap -0.06, learned gate +1.02 at equal 8.20% slow calls; no routed method beat Always-Fast on utility. Yue 2024 shows sample-vote gates at lower cost than verifier gates on GSM8k.]
agent_test: Compare self-confidence gate, random routing and always-fast on cost-adjusted utility.

claim: Planning is not always worth it in LLM tasks: GPT-4o plan-execute-replan raised Event-QA 47.5 to 67.5% but latency 8 s to 317 s; on CMV one-shot was best (60 examples per task, small sample).
agent_test: Per-task-type cost-benefit table; gate from task type.

claim: A fast/slow LLM agent with a rule-based switch (SwiftSage) beat ReAct and Reflexion on ScienceWorld (84.7 vs 36.4 and 45.3) at fewer tokens per action (757 vs 1,971 and 2,983). [Gap search: Swift-only 49.22 vs SwiftSage 62.22 on ScienceWorld (gpt-3.5), so the slow pass adds +13.0; the switch rule uses no tokens.]
agent_test: Reimplement a rule-triggered slow call against always-ReAct at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs show model-based signatures on the two-step task (GPT-3 stay effect; CogBench: size raises model-basedness, step-back +118.59%, CoT +64.59% relative), but this may be partly recall of the known task: retrieval-augmented general LLMs nearly match fine-tuned Centaur (NLL 0.54-0.56 vs 0.51).
agent_test: Measure planning on unseen probes, not the public two-step task.

claim: LLM planning on graph tasks fails when structure must be unrolled: GPT-4 0/30 at temperature 0 and at most 10% at 0.5/1 on shortest path one cluster away in community graphs; BFS/DFS prompting helped some cells.
agent_test: Test explicit-search scaffold vs free CoT on community graphs at equal tokens.

claim: Inside LLMs, sparse-autoencoder features track TD error and Q-values in context (Llama 3 70B, r=0.58; Llama 8B at chance) and successor-representation codes in graph learning.
agent_test: Interpretability only; no direct scaffold test.

claim: Offline replay can do planning work away from decision time (integrates changed rewards), suggesting a consolidation route to cached values.
agent_test: After a task, write summarised plans to memory; test reuse at lower token cost on repeats.

claim: Human cost-benefit arbitration survives proper instructions: Kool 2017 (extensive instructions and comprehension checks) gives d=0.47 (N=98) and d=0.29 (N=93) for stakes raising model-based weight when planning pays, and d=-0.04 (N=100) when it does not. Mean weights stay below 1 (0.40 to 0.65), so the story-instruction result (w near 0.8) does not remove the effect, but no sample has combined story instructions with the payoff-gap design.
agent_test: Test the gate with and without a full task description; check the stakes effect appears only when the slow pass changes accuracy.

claim: Cheap-signal ranking for 'will a slow pass help': on the same 5,000 math items, learned gate (+1.02) > average log-prob (+0.32) > logit gap (-0.06) > random (-1.14) at equal slow-call count (He and Feng 2026, one model pair). On GSM8k, sample-vote routing (acc 0.917 at cost 0.235) beat GPT-3.5 verifier routing (0.884 at 0.253) (Yue 2024). Verbalised confidence is better calibrated than token probability for gpt-3.5 (AUC 0.896 vs 0.869 TriviaQA) but the two were never compared with sample disagreement on the same items.
agent_test: Run one benchmark with three gates on identical items: sample disagreement, mean log-prob, verbalised confidence; score by corrective precision at fixed slow-call rate.

claim: No LLM study tests an explicit expected-gain-versus-token-cost gate against fixed and random routing at equal TOTAL tokens with cost-adjusted utility. Nearest: He and Feng (equal slow-call count; utility of every router below Always-Fast), RaM (trained VOC reward, no routing control), Imagine-then-Plan (adaptive beats fixed and random on a budget curve, no utility table).
agent_test: This is the open experiment for the schema: gate with estimated gain minus token price, equal-token fixed and random arms, report utility.

claim: A break-even exists but is task- and model-specific. Test-time compute pays on easy and medium questions and when inference load is low, but not on the hardest bin (Snell 2024). Planning every step in Crafter cost 3.4 times the tokens of planning every 4 steps for a lower reward (0.349 vs 0.379). Vote-based cascades save cost only if the weak model is good enough (Llama2-13B showed none on GSM8k and CREPE). No LLM study reports a Kool-style payoff-gap curve over token price.
agent_test: Estimate the break-even per task family from a pilot, do not assume a global threshold.

claim: Pattern answers are over-trusted when the task changes (devaluation analogue): counterfactual task variants drop GPT-class accuracy well below default tasks (Wu 2024, 11 pairs); one irrelevant clause drops accuracy up to 65% (Phi-3-mini) and 17.5 to 29.1 points for o1 models (GSM-NoOp); trivial changes flip a false-belief answer (Ullman 2023, P(chocolate)=95% for a transparent bag). No study tests an agent's own cached solution after the task changed.
agent_test: Before reusing a cached answer, run a changed-conditions check (diff the new task against the stored case) and force the slow path when conditions differ.

claim: Gate cost is small relative to savings when the gate is a rule or a small head, but this is rarely measured: SwiftSage's switch uses no tokens and Swift-only already scores 49.22 vs 62.22 with the slow pass; He and Feng's fast pass is 5.26 average tokens against about 519 for the routed system; value-model FLOPs in VGS are 0.024% of generator FLOPs. Snell notes that difficulty estimation itself needs non-trivial compute. Predictor cost in Imagine-then-Plan is not separated from imagination cost (imagination 7.8 s of 14.2 s per step).
agent_test: Log gate tokens separately from slow-pass tokens in any test.

claim: The Goldilocks planning frequency is not stable: the shape of the curve differs by model (Llama-8B degrades sharply with more planning; Gemini Flash degrades on Crafter and POGS) and by environment (TextWorld gains are small); longer-horizon tasks favour larger lookahead (Imagine-then-Plan). No predictive rule was found; RL with a token penalty learns frequency instead.
agent_test: Tune replan frequency per task family; treat a fixed default as a starting point only.

claim: Depth-limited planning with a learned value plug-in helps LLM search at equal generation count (VGS: 39.8 vs 31.6 majority voting, N=256, 12% shorter responses) but no study compares truncated reasoning plus a value estimate against full chain of thought at equal tokens. Human evidence for plan-until-habit is one n=15 vs 15 study with no larger replication.
agent_test: Run truncated reasoning at k tokens plus a cheap value estimate against full CoT at equal total tokens.
